$schema-note: Canonical registry of Owlette's externally scheduled endpoints — the cron-job.org jobs. PATHS + metadata only; secret VALUES never live here, only the NAME of the env var that carries them. Edit this file when you add, remove, retime, or re-auth a scheduled route, then run `npm test -- cronJobs` from web/. See docs/runbooks/talons.md and web/content/docs/setup/web-deployment.mdx.
readme: SOURCE OF TRUTH. This file is the canonical list of every endpoint an EXTERNAL scheduler calls on a timer. If a scheduled route is not listed here, treat it as unregistered.

DRIFT-TESTED. web/__tests__/infra/cronJobs.test.ts fails the build if a route.ts appears under web/app/api/cron/ without an entry here, if an entry points at a route file that no longer exists, or if an entry's declared authHeader no longer appears in its route source. Adding the route is not enough — the registry entry is part of shipping it.

NO SECRETS. Only env var NAMES appear here, in authEnvVar. The values live in the hosting provider and are registered per environment via scripts/env-manifest.json. The drift test scans every string in this file for secret-shaped values and fails on a hit.

PER ENVIRONMENT. Every job must be registered TWICE on cron-job.org — once against dev.owlette.app and once against owlette.app — each carrying that environment's own CRON_SECRET. A prod secret sent to the dev host correctly answers 401 and fires nothing. A registry that lists one job per path under-counts by half.

SILENT BY DEFAULT. Almost every failure mode here is silent: no error, no email, no records, the work simply never happens. An unscheduled job is indistinguishable from a feature nobody configured. Read failureMode before assuming a quiet endpoint is a healthy one.

SCOPE. Externally scheduled HTTP endpoints only. The nine onSchedule Cloud Functions under functions/src are a separate surface, created as a side effect of `firebase deploy --only functions`, and are deliberately not listed here.

scheduler.configLocation: vendor UI only — no repo config, no CLI, no Terraform for these jobs
scheduler.healthyResponse: HTTP 200. 401 means the header name or its value is wrong for that environment. 500 means the handler threw — check the host logs for the route's own log prefix, e.g. `[retention] failed:`. Do not assert on an ok:true body: /api/hoot/escalation answers `success:true` with no ok field at all (route.ts:117), and /api/cron/status-ping derives ok from aggregate component health (route.ts:262), so a successful sweep legitimately reports ok:false while a monitored component is down.
scheduler.note: Not Railway, and not Cloud Scheduler (docs/runbooks/talons.md:105; web/app/api/cron/talons/route.ts:4). Three route docstrings still say 'Railway cron config (set in Railway dashboard)' — health-check:23, process-alerts:21, display-alerts:26. Those are stale; this registry is correct.
scheduler.risk: Free tier, no SLA. If cron-job.org stops quietly, health alerts, status pings, and talon dispatch stop with it until someone notices by hand (docs/roadmap.md:15).

dev.authEnvVarSource: the dev value of CRON_SECRET (target railway-dev in scripts/env-manifest.json)

prod.servedBy: Railway service owlette-prod, fronted by the Cloudflare failover load balancer
prod.authEnvVarSource: the prod value of CRON_SECRET (target railway-prod in scripts/env-manifest.json)

jobs.purpose: Scans every site and machine for stale heartbeats past OFFLINE_THRESHOLD_MS (5 minutes, route.ts:33), debounces with a per-machine staleSince marker (STALE_CONFIRM_MS, route.ts:55), aggregates per site behind a settling window, then sends one consolidated 'machines offline' email per site, fires machine.offline webhooks, taps the talon matcher with the machine_offline event, and clears stale rebooting/shuttingDown latches at the source.

failureMode.description: Nobody is ever emailed that a machine went offline, machine.offline webhooks never fire, and machine_offline talons never fire at all — this route is the only dispatcher for that event, since an offline machine cannot report its own absence. Stale rebooting/shuttingDown latches are also never cleared, so a machine that shut down cleanly or failed a reboot keeps pulsing the 'restarting' status pill for every client indefinitely.

jobs.detectedBy: nothing — no status component and no watchdog covers this route
jobs.note: Runtime is genuinely unbounded: it iterates every site, then every machine within it, with serial Firestore writes and serial per-recipient sends. Runtime scales with fleet size and there is no internal cap, which is why the timeout floor is 60s rather than the default.

jobs.purpose: Drains the pending_process_alerts queue after a 2-minute accumulation window (ACCUMULATION_WINDOW_MS, route.ts:28), groups by site, filters per-recipient muted machines, sends one digest email per recipient with an individual unsubscribe link, then deletes the processed queue documents in batches.

failureMode.description: The agent only queues process crash and start-failure alerts; this route is what turns them into email. Unscheduled, the queue grows without bound and no operator is ever notified of a crashed process.

jobs.detectedBy: the alert_delivery status component (web/lib/healthChecks.server.ts:277) counts stale pending_process_alerts and degrades — published by /api/cron/status-ping. alert_delivery is also the only component whose degrade transition pages Sentry (SENTRY_ALERTING_COMPONENTS, status-ping/route.ts:22).

jobs.purpose: Same shape as process-alerts, for the pending_display_alerts queue: drains display and monitor events older than the 2-minute accumulation window (ACCUMULATION_WINDOW_MS, route.ts:39), groups by site, respects the displayAlerts opt-out and per-user mutedMachines, and emails one digest per recipient.

failureMode.description: Display drift, monitor-config change, and similar events are queued and never emailed.

jobs.detectedBy: the alert_delivery status component (web/lib/healthChecks.server.ts:277) counts stale pending_display_alerts and degrades — published by /api/cron/status-ping
jobs.note: Two display events bypass this queue on purpose and email inline from /api/agent/alert: display_monitor_removed and display_auto_revert_fired. They are unaffected by this job's schedule.

jobs.purpose: Runs the nine status components (dashboard, api, agent_registry, webhook_delivery, alert_delivery, talon_dispatch, r2_uploads, firestore, cortex_chat), writes a status_pings document, computes degrade and recover transitions against the two previous pings, publishes component status to Instatus, and raises a Sentry event on the degrade transition for alert_delivery only (SENTRY_ALERTING_COMPONENTS, route.ts:22).

failureMode.description: The public status page freezes at whatever it last showed, and the two stall detectors that exist only inside this route — alert_delivery for a stuck digest cron, talon_dispatch for a stuck talon sweep — never run, so a second failed cron produces no signal at all. Sentry never fires for a degraded alert pipeline.

jobs.detectedBy: nothing — this route IS the watchdog for the others, so its own failure is unobserved except by the status page going stale
jobs.note: Its own response body reports fleet health, not job health: ok mirrors whether all nine components passed (route.ts:262), so judge this job by the 200 alone. Instatus publishing also degrades quietly when a component id env var is missing — setInstatusComponentStatus returns skipped rather than throwing (instatusClient.ts:104), so the route still answers 200 while that component never updates. Verify with `node scripts/check-status-page-ready.mjs`.

jobs.purpose: Deletes metrics_history buckets by document-id range and site logs by indexed timestamp, past a 400-day window (METRICS_RETENTION_DAYS / LOGS_RETENTION_DAYS). Bounded at MAX_DELETES_PER_RUN = 2000 documents per invocation (route.ts:59), oldest-first so progress is monotonic across runs.

failureMode.description: Nothing errors, but data past 400 days is retained forever, which contradicts the retention commitment in the privacy policy section 6 — the route's own header comment states this job is the only thing enforcing that claim. Deliberately not a Firestore TTL policy, so there is no fallback mechanism.

jobs.detectedBy: nothing — read the response body instead: truncated:true means the run hit its 2000-document ceiling and older data still remains
jobs.note: Against a large first-time backlog, schedule hourly until a run reports truncated:false, then drop back to daily. Any quiet hour works; 04:00 is the documented default.

jobs.purpose: Sweeps sites/{siteId}/machines/{machineId}/swoop_sessions. First closes records still marked pending or live past their absolute 12-hour cap — sessions nobody closed, because the browser went away without its teardown landing — then deletes every session document that started more than SWOOP_SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS (30) ago. Bounded at 200 closes and 2000 deletes per invocation, oldest-first so progress is monotonic across runs.

failureMode.description: Nothing errors. Session documents accumulate forever, each naming the user who started the session and every viewer uid in it — who watched which machine, when — with no other deletion path, since this collection is deliberately not covered by a Firestore TTL policy. Abandoned records also keep answering as live to the revocation sweep, so every later membership change re-kills sessions that ended months ago.

jobs.detectedBy: nothing — read the response body instead: truncated:true means the run hit a ceiling or a delete exhausted its retries, and records remain. A steadily non-zero closed count means sessions are ending without anything closing them, which is a bug upstream of this job, not a healthy sweep.
jobs.note: Separate from cron-retention on purpose: that job's 400-day window is the public commitment for operational history, and this collection is not history — the audit trail for a session lives in sites/{siteId}/audit_log, which a site admin cannot delete. Scheduled 30 minutes after cron-retention so the two daily sweeps do not overlap; any quiet time works.

jobs.purpose: Collection-group scan of every user's api_keys for documents whose expiresAt falls between 24 hours ago and EXPIRATION_WARNING_MS ahead (14 days, web/lib/apiKeyTypes.ts), assigns each the smallest unfired rung of the 14 / 3 / 0 day ladder, skips rotated and revoked keys, then stamps expiryNoticedStages on the owner's own key document BEFORE sending one email per owner listing all their expiring keys.

failureMode.description: Nobody is ever warned that an api key is about to expire. The first symptom is a 401 in whatever integration held the key — a CI pipeline, an SDK caller, a customer's automation — with nothing in owlette indicating why. The dashboard's amber 'expiring soon' row still renders, so the information exists; it just never leaves the app.

jobs.detectedBy: nothing — no status component covers this route. Read the response body: keysScanned is non-zero on any fleet with live keys, and usersNotified exceeding emailsSent means recipients opted out, were deleted, or a send failed.
jobs.note: Any hour works — the ladder is measured in whole days from expiresAt, not against wall-clock time. Each rung is stamped before its email is sent, so a duplicate registration or a scheduler retry cannot re-send a rung; the accepted cost is that a send failing after the stamp loses that one notice, and the next rung down still fires.

jobs.purpose: The talon scheduler sweep, and the only thing that fires a schedule-triggered talon. Three passes per run: close out runs abandoned mid-flight, fire delayed event triggers whose runAfterAt has come due, then claim due schedules transactionally so two overlapping sweeps cannot double-fire. Anything more than MISSED_FIRE_GRACE_MS (10 minutes, route.ts:82) late is recorded as a missed run rather than executed, so a stalled scheduler does not replay an hour of automations on recovery.

failureMode.description: No error, no email, no run records — every scheduled talon simply never fires, and a talon that stopped firing looks identical to a talon nobody configured. Pending deferrals past their 10-minute grace are written off permanently.

jobs.detectedBy: the talon_dispatch status component (web/lib/healthChecks.server.ts:321), published by /api/cron/status-ping
jobs.note: The only route with an explicit wall-clock budget: SWEEP_BUDGET_MS is 50_000 ms (route.ts:74), with 25 claims and 25 deferral claims per sweep. A healthy sweep may use up to ~50s, so the scheduler timeout must be at least 60s or a good run gets cut off mid-flight.

jobs.purpose: Backstop poller for autonomous hoot. Scans every site's cortex-events subcollection for documents flagged escalationPending, sends the escalation email via Resend, and clears the flag regardless of send outcome. The flag is written by the agent (write_escalation_flag in agent/src/cortex_firestore.py) and this route is its only reader.

failureMode.description: Escalation emails are never sent and escalationPending stays true forever on those event documents. Only matters where autonomous hoot is enabled; the docs frame the route as a backstop, so a missed run delays rather than loses escalations — but with the route entirely unscheduled there is no other drain.

alias.note: Back-compat re-export of the same handlers, kept because the shipped @owlette/cli and the SDKs still call the old path. Existing schedules pointing at it keep working; register anything new against the canonical /api/hoot/ path. Do not list it as a separate job.

jobs.note: THE ODD ONE OUT, twice over. It reads the Authorization header as `Bearer <CRON_SECRET>`, not X-Cron-Secret; sending the wrong header shape returns 401 with no other symptom. The GET handler strips the prefix with an unanchored replace, so a bare value also authenticates — do not rely on that. It is also the one job that does not answer with an ok field: a healthy run returns `success:true` (route.ts:117). The POST handler in the same file is a different surface entirely (x-cortex-secret against CORTEX_INTERNAL_SECRET, server-to-server) and is not scheduled.
